A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk of upper GI bleeding is reduced by H pylori eradication, NSAID avoidance, PPIs and COX-2 inhibitors, and beta-blockers and ligation in patients with oesophageal varices.
the risk of GI bleeding can be significantly reduced in patients taking antiplatelet drugs or NSAIDs by using appropriate strategies to prevent peptic ulceration.
in patients with a history of peptic ulcer disease or previous GI bleeding and in patients with high cardiovascular risk, a COX-1 sparing NSAID plus PPI combination would be the best strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in patients who need antiplatelet therapy, the risk of GI bleeding is high and should be taken into consideration.
the risk of upper GI bleeding is not the same for all patients, and therefore a risk-based approach is needed to prevent this complication.
there is no one size fits all approach for the prevention of GI bleeding in patients taking antiplatelet drugs.
